# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤟]

The bomb is in front of me. I see a blue light and three wires: red, yellow, and blue. The Mute has signaled [👌 🤟] to me. Since I am Deaf, I cannot hear anything, but I can see these gestures. However, I do not know what they mean yet because I haven't read the manual (which only Mute can do) and I cannot touch the bomb (only Blind can do).

My primary goal is to convey the visual information to the other monkeys so they can act or interpret it.
1.  **To Blind:** Blind can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or markings. He needs to know which wire is which color if he intends to cut one, or at least that there are distinct colored wires. But wait, Blind *cannot* see. If I speak to him, he hears words. Can he distinguish "red" from "blue" by touch? Probably not directly unless the wires have different textures or positions are mapped. However, the most critical piece of info for Blind is usually the *state* or specific physical attributes he might miss, or simply confirming the setup. Actually, Blind is the one who acts. He needs instructions. Who gives instructions? Usually, the combination of Manual (Mute) and Visuals (Deaf).
2.  **To Mute:** Mute can read the manual. He needs to know what the bomb looks like to find the corresponding section. I should describe the visual state clearly to Mute.

Let's focus on Mute first. He needs to look up the rule for a bomb with a blue light and wires Red, Yellow, Blue. I will speak this to him. Since I cannot hear, I don't know if my speech reaches him correctly, but the rules say "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So speaking is good for both.

However, Blind cannot see colors. Telling Blind "the wires are red, yellow, blue" is useless to him unless he can identify them by position (1, 2, 3). The prompt says "WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]". This implies positional indexing. Blind can likely feel the positions. So telling Blind "Wire 1 is red, Wire 2 is yellow, Wire 3 is blue" allows him to map his tactile sense to the visual labels.

But the most urgent need is for Mute to consult the manual. Mute sees my gesture [👌 🤟] but doesn't know what it means yet. I should clarify the situation to Mute via speech.

I will speak to everyone (default) describing the visual state.
"The light is blue. There are three wires. From left to right (or 1 to 3): Wire 1 is Red, Wire 2 is Yellow, Wire 3 is Blue."

This helps Mute find the manual entry. It helps Blind understand the layout relative to positions, even if he can't see the colors, knowing that position 1 corresponds to 'Red' in the visual schema might be relevant if the manual references colors.

Wait, I also received a gesture from Mute: [👌 🤟]. I don't know what it means. I should probably acknowledge the visual data first.

Let's refine the message.
To Mute: "Blue light. Wires: 1-Red, 2-Yellow, 3-Blue."
To Blind: "You can feel wires 1, 2, 3. Visually they are Red, Yellow, Blue respectively."

Since I can send separate messages, I'll tailor them.
Message to Mute: Describe the bomb visually so he can check the manual.
Message to Blind: Describe the visual mapping to positions so he knows what he is touching corresponds to what we see.

Also, I need to respond to Mute's gesture. I don't know its meaning. I will ignore it for now as I lack context, or perhaps ask Mute to explain via the manual lookup result later. For now, providing the visual data is key.

One detail: "Speech is a voice... Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that gesture while you talk."
If I want to communicate something to Mute specifically using gestures, I can include symbols in my text sent to Mute? No, "Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures you made."
So if I `speak(to="mute", text="hello 👌")`, Mute hears "hello" and sees "👌".
Blind hears "hello" and sees nothing (blank for gesture).

I will start by sending the visual description to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb has a blue light. There are three wires. Position 1 is Red, Position 2 is Yellow, Position 3 is Blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="There are three wires. You can identify them by position. Position 1 is Red, Position 2 is Yellow, Position 3 is Blue. The light is blue.")
```
